===== FILE .claude/skills/defi-footguns/SKILL.md | SOURCE SHA256 5090b32ab6ff62df0a21d945bd85174eb0dfbb76639dda1e3489add8365470df | RENDERING verbatim =====
---
name: defi-footguns
description: Use when touching anything in this repo that verifies, checks, gates, or reports a result - paper/build.sh, formal/v3/*gate*, totalgate.mjs, negtest-*.sh, the sigma gates, or any script that compares a figure against paper/atlas.tex. Also use when a checker reports success, when adding an assertion, or when deciding how many review rounds a change needs.
---

# DeFi footguns

Traps that have actually fired in this repository, with the evidence. Every
entry below was measured, not predicted.

**Core principle: this repo's gates exist to stop a confident wrong answer.
Every trap here is a gate that produced one — usually about something it had
not measured.**

Read `formal/v3/GATE-REGISTER.md` alongside this: it records, per gate, whether
it has ever been *observed* failing. Two gates are marked `CANNOT FAIL` and are
still cited as verification commands in `AGENDA-COMPLETE.md`.

## Quick reference

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD FAILED: a headline total disagrees with the verdicts`, but the PDFs rendered and the totals are right | `paper/build.sh` discarded the gate's stderr with `>/dev/null 2>&1` and mapped **every** nonzero exit onto one editorial sentence | Branch on the exit code: `0` holds, `1` the property is false, `3` the check could not run. Never merge those |
| A gate reports `PASS` / `ok` / `agree` after examining nothing | Empty glob, empty directory, zero-iteration loop. `verify_final.py` printed `X21-armed pairs: 0 of 0` and exited 0 on every tree but the author's | A zero denominator is a **blocked** check, exit 3. Print the denominator in the result line |
| Running the verification suite leaves the repo dirty | Gate scripts write their result JSON back into the tree, so *verifying* and *regenerating* are the same action and a gate can never disagree with its own record | Snapshot `git status --porcelain -uall` before and after. If a gate rewrites its evidence, diff it — reproducing bit-for-bit except a recorded absolute path is genuine |
| `quint typecheck` cited as verification | It checks types and effects. It never evaluates `init`, never steps, never reads an invariant. **0 of 92 `.qnt` files declare an `invariant`, `temporal` or `run`** — `quint test` is an empty suite everywhere | Name the property: `quint run <f> --invariant=inv_all`. Expect `usd1.qnt` to go red — it ships violating `inv_supply` |
| A gate shell reports `FAIL 61 of 72` about a corpus it never read | Unguarded `cd`, or a harness truncated with `head`/`tail` **before** being judged, discarding the EACCES that marks a blocked run | `cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." \|\| exit 3`, plus a sentinel checking real content. Capture output in full; truncate only for display |
| A `cd` guard is present and the script still lies | `cd` into a directory that merely **exists** succeeds. Landing in `/tmp` is not a failure | Sentinel on content: `corpus50/lanes/*.json` present, `begin{measurement}` in `atlas.tex` |
| A count of blocked checks is off by one | `grep -c 'BLOCKED'` also matches the `GATE RESULT: BLOCKED` summary line | Anchor: `grep -cE '^  BLOCKED'`. This is the repo's own canonical example — `grep -q "violation"` matches Quint's success string `[ok] No violation found` |
| A figure "agrees" with the paper but the paper is wrong | `has()` was `tex.includes()` over a 151 KB document. Strip the approx markers and `strict` becomes `45.3`, satisfied by the **coverage** literal eleven lines above | Anchor each figure to the block *and* the sentence that asserts it, and require every site that states it to agree |
| An anchored claim search finds the wrong text | A `\label` sits wherever the author put it — near the top of a `measurement`, but inside the **caption** of a `table`, *below* the tabular body. Slicing forward from the label misses the numbers | Bound the block by `\begin{env}`…`\end{env}`, not by the label's position |
| A comment or an unused macro satisfies a claim | A LaTeX comment is never typeset; nor is an uninvoked `\newcommand` body, nor the untaken branch of a conditional | Strip comments (see parity below). For conditionals, **refuse rather than resolve** — see the wiki. There is no complete fix short of reading the typeset PDF |
| Comment stripping misses `\\%` | LaTeX comment semantics are backslash **parity**: `\%` is a literal percent, `\\%` is a line break followed by a **live** comment. A single-preceding-character test keeps the second | `replace(/(^\|[^\\])((?:\\\\)*)%.*$/gm, "$1$2")` — consume the pairs |
| A conditional check blocks a correct paper | `\iff` (the math operator) matches a naive `\\if[a-zA-Z]*` | Match the real primitives: `ifnum ifdim ifodd ifx iftrue iffalse ifcase ifdefined ifcsname else fi` |
| Every fix is defeated by the symmetric case one step away | Four consecutive rounds closed a pole and left its dual: whole-document → block-scoped missing a second site; comment stripped → wrong parity; `\iffalse` stripped → `\iftrue` untouched | When a fix is about *which* form, ask what the other polarity is **before** shipping. Better: make the check refuse ambiguity rather than resolve it |
| A "guard" passes on an arithmetically impossible input | The total row `total & --- & 1259 & 570 & 689 & 15` was checked by testing each number occurred *somewhere* in the table. Permuting to `1259 & 689 & 570 & 15` passed | Cells carry meaning by **position**. Read the row as a row |
| A count-based guard misses a partial corpus | Zero-file guards say nothing about four files of five, and "is an array" says nothing about `[]` | Count what you visited and refuse to compare an incomplete corpus. Better: make two independent sources check **each other** — `tot` from verdicts vs obligation items from specs; `cov` vs `assigned` |

## The assertion traps — the most expensive class here

Four distinct ways an assertion stayed green against reverted code, all observed
in this repo:

1. **It tests a copy.** The probe re-implemented `want()` / `blocked_out()` in a
   heredoc, so reverting the real hunk left it exercising a private copy that
   still had the fix. Lift the function from source with a **bounded** extractor.
2. **It greps source instead of running behaviour.** A check for
   `case "$brc" in` passed against a block that was dead code after an `exit`.
3. **A parent guard already returns the same code.** The per-verdict
   `Number.isFinite` check sat under an existing `tot === 0` guard, so the
   fixture returned 3 either way. Lock by the specific **message**.
4. **The fixture is degenerate.** A one-slug corpus can't exhibit a
   silent-skip: the `tot === 0` guard fires first. **Two slugs minimum** for
   anything about a partial walk.

**Every guard needs a positive control** proving it fires on a defeating input,
**and** a negative one proving it isn't always-on. A dot-terminated sentence
window shipped that failed the *intact* corpus — its control was the only reason
it didn't ship red.

## A bounded function lift

`awk '/^fn\(\) \{/,/^\}/'` runs on to the **next** function's closing brace when
the definition is one-lined, so `tail -1 == "}"` passes on swallowed script body
(measured: 40 lines, 5 of them body, lift returned 0). Require: non-empty, ends
`}`, contains exactly one `^name() {`, and no line matching `^(echo|one |want "|===== )`.

## How many review rounds

**State the threat model in the brief.** This repo ran 21 adversarial rounds.
Rounds 1–11 found real defects — the published lie in four places, a silent
PASS, gates that could not fail. Rounds 12–21 found manuscript mutations that
require an adversary with **write access to `atlas.tex`**, which is not the
threat: the real risk is a collaborator regenerating one figure and missing
another.

- Budget rounds up front. Extension is an explicit decision, not a default.
- Tell reviewers to rank by **realistic likelihood**, not constructibility.
- **You** decide what blocks shipping. A finding needing adversarial write
  access to the artifact under test is a note, not a blocker.
- Tripwire: N consecutive rounds touching the same files → stop and reassess.
  Here, ten consecutive commits touched the same two files.

## Common mistakes

- **Trusting a gate's summary line.** `all headline totals agree with the
  verdicts` was printed while two of the four cells in the row it named were
  never compared.
- **Believing a stated limitation.** A limitation is a claim like any other.
  `GATE-REGISTER.md` overstated its own bound twice and a reviewer caught it
  both times.
- **Reading only the last line.** `one()` judged on `tail -1`, discarding the
  evidence that marks a blocked run — in a file whose own header says every
  check greps the whole output.

## Adding entries

Append only footguns that actually fired, symptom first — that is what a future
reader searches for. Keep the quick-reference table the primary surface. Record
the measurement, not the intuition.

---
name: openspec-propose
description: Propose a new change with all artifacts generated in one step. Use when the user wants to quickly describe what they want to build and get a complete proposal with design, specs, and tasks ready for implementation.
allowed-tools: Bash(openspec:*)
license: MIT
compatibility: Requires openspec CLI.
metadata:
  author: openspec
  version: "1.0"
  generatedBy: "1.6.0"
---

Propose a new change - create the change and generate all artifacts in one step.

I'll create a change with artifacts:
- proposal.md (what & why)
- design.md (how)
- tasks.md (implementation steps)

When ready to implement, run /opsx:apply

---

**Store selection:** If the user names a store (a store is a standalone OpenSpec repo registered on this machine) or the work lives in one, run `openspec store list --json` to discover registered store ids, then pass `--store <id>` on the commands that read or write specs and changes (`new change`, `status`, `instructions`, `list`, `show`, `validate`, `archive`, `doctor`, `context`). Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

**Input**: The user's request should include a change name (kebab-case) OR a description of what they want to build.

**Steps**

1. **If no clear input provided, ask what they want to build**

   Use the **AskUserQuestion tool** (open-ended, no preset options) to ask:
   > "What change do you want to work on? Describe what you want to build or fix."

   From their description, derive a kebab-case name (e.g., "add user authentication" → `add-user-auth`).

   **IMPORTANT**: Do NOT proceed without understanding what the user wants to build.

2. **Create the change directory**
   ```bash
   openspec new change "<name>"
   ```
   This creates a scaffolded change in the planning home resolved by the CLI with `.openspec.yaml`.

3. **Get the artifact build order**
   ```bash
   openspec status --change "<name>" --json
   ```
   Parse the JSON to get:
   - `applyRequires`: array of artifact IDs needed before implementation (e.g., `["tasks"]`)
   - `artifacts`: list of all artifacts with their status and dependencies
   - `planningHome`, `changeRoot`, `artifactPaths`, and `actionContext`: path and scope context. Use these instead of assuming repo-local paths.

4. **Create artifacts in sequence until apply-ready**

   Use the **TodoWrite tool** to track progress through the artifacts.

   Loop through artifacts in dependency order (artifacts with no pending dependencies first):

   a. **For each artifact that is `ready` (dependencies satisfied)**:
      - Get instructions:
        ```bash
        openspec instructions <artifact-id> --change "<name>" --json
        ```
      - The instructions JSON includes:
        - `context`: Project background (constraints for you - do NOT include in output)
        - `rules`: Artifact-specific rules (constraints for you - do NOT include in output)
        - `template`: The structure to use for your output file
        - `instruction`: Schema-specific guidance for this artifact type
        - `resolvedOutputPath`: Resolved path or pattern to write the artifact
        - `dependencies`: Completed artifacts to read for context
      - Read any completed dependency files for context
      - Create the artifact file using `template` as the structure and write it to `resolvedOutputPath`
      - Apply `context` and `rules` as constraints - but do NOT copy them into the file
      - Show brief progress: "Created <artifact-id>"

   b. **Continue until all `applyRequires` artifacts are complete**
      - After creating each artifact, re-run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`
      - Check if every artifact ID in `applyRequires` has `status: "done"` in the artifacts array
      - Stop when all `applyRequires` artifacts are done

   c. **If an artifact requires user input** (unclear context):
      - Use **AskUserQuestion tool** to clarify
      - Then continue with creation

5. **Show final status**
   ```bash
   openspec status --change "<name>"
   ```

**Output**

After completing all artifacts, summarize:
- Change name and location
- List of artifacts created with brief descriptions
- What's ready: "All artifacts created! Ready for implementation."
- Prompt: "Run `/opsx:apply` or ask me to implement to start working on the tasks."

**Artifact Creation Guidelines**

- Follow the `instruction` field from `openspec instructions` for each artifact type
- The schema defines what each artifact should contain - follow it
- Read dependency artifacts for context before creating new ones
- Use `template` as the structure for your output file - fill in its sections
- **IMPORTANT**: `context` and `rules` are constraints for YOU, not content for the file
  - Do NOT copy `<context>`, `<rules>`, `<project_context>` blocks into the artifact
  - These guide what you write, but should never appear in the output

**Guardrails**
- Create ALL artifacts needed for implementation (as defined by schema's `apply.requires`)
- Always read dependency artifacts before creating a new one
- If context is critically unclear, ask the user - but prefer making reasonable decisions to keep momentum
- If a change with that name already exists, ask if user wants to continue it or create a new one
- Verify each artifact file exists after writing before proceeding to next

# Provisional normalized corpus

This is the source-bound corpus increment of the semantic-kernel migration.
It preserves the 72 historical records in `corpus50/lanes` and maps them to 75
candidate units. Liquity's bundled row is split into V1/V2; Ondo's bundled row
is split into USDY, OUSG and Global Markets. Other product/version bundles and
all deployment identities remain unresolved. This is a development corpus.

The proposal's linked CSV and JSON Schema were not recovered. These files are
new reconstructions; they do not reproduce its absent annotations or the stated
31/72 multi-function count. A valid generated dataset means the reconstruction
is complete and consistent with its declared inputs, not that its financial
classifications or source claims have been verified.

## Reproduce and check

From the repository root, using Python and the dependency version in
`corpus/normalized/requirements.txt`:

Check the committed corpus (actual independent annotations):

```sh
python3 scripts/corpus_normalize.py check --repo .
```

Reproduce it in a new directory and check that output:

```sh
python3 scripts/corpus_normalize.py build --repo . --out /tmp/corpus-build-NEW
python3 scripts/corpus_normalize.py check --repo . --data /tmp/corpus-build-NEW
```

Run the separate CLI regression suite:

```sh
python3 scripts/test_corpus_normalize.py
```

The regression suite constructs synthetic annotations in temporary repositories.
Its agreement counts are fixture values; they are not the actual corpus results.
The actual integration evidence records the first command and a byte comparison
of all three regenerated files separately.

`build` requires a new output directory. It emits `corpus.json`, `crosswalk.csv`
and `coverage.json`. `check` defaults to `corpus/normalized/generated` and accepts
`--data DIR` for another output directory. It checks without regenerating files.
Exit 0 means a complete, nonempty and internally consistent provisional corpus;
exit 1 means invalid derived data or annotations; exit 3 means required evidence
could not be checked. A missing generated output is not a successful empty check. JSON Schema alone
is not an acceptance gate: `check` must also enforce identity, provenance,
set operations and exact derived bytes. Argument syntax errors retain argparse
status 2; the 0/1/3 contract applies to valid build/check invocations.

## What is preserved

- Source file byte hashes, source commit and JSON pointers bind every original
  record, including rank statements, ordering, residue and forced-fit notes.
- Organization IDs are corpus-label containers. Shared Jupiter, Maple and
  Steakhouse labels do not merge their product-context records or prove common
  deployment/legal identity.
- Version labels are distinct from deployed bytecode/source-code revisions.
  Every chain/address/revision remains unresolved here. IDs are stable within
  this frozen inventory, not a universal external entity-resolution service.
- Split children reference the original row as bundled context. Its complete
  mechanism, residue and forced-fit arrays are not asserted for every child.

## Annotation and disagreement

Two separate GPT-6 contexts receive the same neutral annotation input and
controlled taxonomy. Neither reads the other's output. Their files record the
actual input hash and remain separate. This is independent elicitation from the
same model family, not independent human expert verification.

Each candidate has economic-function, instrument, mechanism, execution and trust
facets. The rationale and uncertainty remain available in the raw annotation
files. Empty labels mean not evidenced or unresolved, not proved absence.
Identical label sets are provisional agreement. Different sets retain their
intersection provisionally; the symmetric difference is explicitly unresolved
under a reusable rule. Intersection does not settle the disagreement.

Coverage reports count these decisions and missing identities. Agreement counts
separate matching nonempty label sets from matching empty sets; the latter
record mutual non-evidence. They do not
measure semantic accuracy, generalization, protocol fidelity or kernel adequacy.
No unit in this corpus is an untouched holdout.

Native review also challenged the agreed Liquity V1 `liquidation` label as
insufficiently grounded in child-specific text. It remains an observed model
agreement, with an open source-evidence challenge recorded in the sprint review;
it must not be treated as a verified mechanism classification.

## Provenance boundaries

`inputs/source-manifest.json` binds the three historical files and preserves
their own source statements. Their August 2026 rankings and narrative claims
are not newly fetched, re-ranked or certified by this sprint.

`sources/primary-excerpts.json` records a separate September retrieval of limited
primary documentation excerpts and response fingerprints. These corroborate
named version/product distinctions only. They are not inputs to the historical
blind coding and do not supply deployment addresses or code revisions. Full HTTP
responses were retained in a temporary local capture; the durable artifact is
the excerpt and response fingerprint, not a complete archived page.

The captured V1 page URL and the V2 excerpt provide the version naming; the
retained V1 excerpt itself is unversioned. The official [Liquity V1 documentation](https://docs.liquity.org/liquity-v1) and
[Liquity V2 documentation](https://docs.liquity.org/) distinguish those versions.
[Ondo's documentation](https://docs.ondo.finance/) distinguishes USDY and OUSG.
Its current navigation uses Ondo Stocks; this reconstruction retains the legacy
Global Markets label without asserting a rename or deployment equivalence.

Further source acquisition must resolve deployments, remaining bundled products,
classification disagreements and protocol-dependency edges before this can serve
as a deployment benchmark. See the [sprint design](../../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-corpus-provenance-design.md)
for acceptance scope and the [migration ledger](../../docs/research/semantic-kernel-progress.md)
for verification and review results.

So the contested symbol is load-bearing and I use it. But it under-resolves badly: Ve as defined names a non-transferable time-decaying lock and nothing else, while Curve runs four separable mechanisms on that lock (lock, gauge weight vote, LP boost, external bribe market), three of which are listed above as residue. Ve should be demoted from a symbol to a family."},{"symbol":"St","why":"FORCED: St covers the stableswap pools (the majority of TVL) but not the tricrypto/twocrypto pools, whose invariant is the unnamed repegging curve above."},{"symbol":"Fd","why":"CANDIDATE: admin fees are converted and distributed to veCRV lockers — one of the few genuine distributions to a claim class in this whole lane, so the fit is good; marked only because Fd is a candidate."},{"symbol":"Ag","why":"FORCED: the on-chain router/registry constructs multi-pool routes within Curve only. Including it makes Aave look like a CDP protocol; excluding it deletes a real liability."},{"symbol":"Rb","why":"FORCED: aTokens are scaled balances times an index — internally Ix, externally Rb. This is the largest single unnamed business in the lane.","no element for immutability as a positive commitment: Morpho Blue has no admin and cannot be upgraded. Sky's D3M / Spark Liquidity Layer mints USDS directly into SparkLend to hold the borrow rate at a governance-set target. The lender is the issuer of the borrowed asset, the supply is created on demand, and the objective is a rate not a yield. This is a central bank's discount window and the vocabulary has nothing: not Pl (no depositor), not Em (nothing is emitted), not Ps (no 1:1 reserve swap), not Cd (no per-position collateral).","same interest-rate-model residue as Aave V3 — and it bites harder here, because the whole protocol exists to peg one rate","no element for a fork's dependence on its upstream (Spark inherits Aave V3's security assumptions and patch cadence)"]},"pointer":"/categories/1/protocols/2","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane1-dex-lending-cdp-lsd.json","source_sha256":"afaf18d717dbd0ccc4e2909c146943e37ed3dff3c982bcfbc9b4f71f26c23369"},{"category":"Lending","legacy_id":"legacy:lane1:c1:p3","original":{"elements":["Pl","Sh","Ix","Ct","Ex","Li","Em","Up","Gp"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Sh","why":"FORCED: jTokens are pro-rata claims whose value moves via a rising exchange rate — the mechanism is Ix and the user-facing object is Sh. As with Aave's aTokens, the vocabulary charges two symbols for one design."},{"symbol":"Li","why":"FORCED: correct in substance, but silent on the close factor and the seize-vs-repay split that define how Compound-family liquidation actually behaves."}],"name":"JustLend V1","order_known":true,"rank_basis":"$3,385.2M TVL, DefiLlama 2026-08-04, rank 4","residue":["no element for the TRX energy/bandwidth rental market JustLend also operates — renting a chain resource rather than capital. No element distinguishes 'issuer holds reserves' from 'custodian holds reserves for issuer', which is a material creditor-priority difference.","Governance/ownership concentration and related-party dealing as a solvency-relevant fact.","The token is deployed natively on multiple chains by the issuer, again not `Xf`."]},"pointer":"/categories/2/protocols/2","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Reserve-backed / fiat stablecoin issuers","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c2:p3","original":{"elements":["Ps","Rd","At","Fz","Fd","Up"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Ps","why":"off-chain mint/redeem."},{"symbol":"Fd","why":"candidate register, and forced: the surplus distribution is a legal agreement executed by wire, not an on-chain fee flow. Used only to record that a distribution exists at all."},{"symbol":"Fz","why":"candidate register: Paxos holds and uses freeze authority."}],"name":"Global Dollar USDG (Paxos / Global Dollar Network)","order_known":false,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama stablecoins $3.42B circulating 2026-08-04 (#4 among fiat-backed)","residue":["The distinguishing feature of USDG is a RESERVE-YIELD SHARING AGREEMENT with distribution partners (exchanges, wallets) based on held balances. This is a contractual off-chain revenue split computed from on-chain balances; `Fd` names on-chain surplus distribution and is a poor fit.","The NYDFS trust charter and the segregated-reserve requirements that make USDG legally different from USDT. Unnameable.","Same reserve/obligor/banking residue as every other member.","No element for a CONSORTIUM as an issuer governance form — the network's members jointly determine allocation policy."]},"pointer":"/categories/2/protocols/3","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Reserve-backed / fiat stablecoin issuers","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c2:p4","original":{"elements":["Ps","Rd","At","Fz","Xm","Xf","Up"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Ps","why":"off-chain mint/redeem by Paxos."},{"symbol":"Xm","why":"the LayerZero OFT deployment to Solana/Arbitrum is genuine cross-domain messaging, but the ETHEREUM supply is native issuance, so PYUSD is simultaneously natively multi-issued and bridge-extended and the two are indistinguishable in this vocabulary."},{"symbol":"Fz","why":"candidate register: Paxos freeze/wipe authority."}],"name":"PayPal USD (PYUSD)","order_known":false,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama stablecoins $2.68B circulating 2026-08-04 (#5 among fiat-backed)","residue":["The dominant PYUSD use path is INSIDE PAYPAL'S CUSTODIAL LEDGER — a closed-loop database where PYUSD converts 1:1 to a PayPal balance. Most PYUSD activity is not on-chain at all, and there is no element for 'a custodial off-chain ledger that shadows the token'.","Same reserve/obligor/banking residue; issued by Paxos Trust under NYDFS.","No element for a CONSUMER PAYMENT NETWORK as the demand source (merchant settlement, chargeback semantics, dispute reversal) — chargebacks are a forced-reversal primitive that the on-chain token cannot support and the wrapper must.","Reserve yield accrues to PayPal, plus a promotional rewards rate paid to holders out of it — an issuer-funded yield with no `Em` character (not protocol emissions, marketing spend)."]},"pointer":"/categories/2/protocols/4","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Prediction markets & other (uncategorized large protocols)","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c3:p0","original":{"elements":["Aw","Rd","Ct"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Rd","why":"contracts settle to $1 or $0, which resembles redemption, but the settlement is a clearinghouse bookkeeping entry against a segregated account, not a redemption right against reserves."},{"symbol":"Ct","why":"margin exists for multi-leg and short positions, but it is exchange-rule margin computed off-chain by the DCO, not the on-chain health computation `Ct` describes."},{"symbol":"Aw","why":"KYC/geographic eligibility is an account-opening process at a regulated broker, not a transfer gate."}],"name":"Kalshi","order_known":false,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama $10.89B volume/30d 2026-08-04 — #1 prediction market by 3.5x, and larger by volume than any other protocol in my entire lane except the stablecoins","residue":["A CENTRAL COUNTERPARTY. Kalshi operates a CFTC-registered DCO that NOVATES every trade and stands between buyer and seller. There is no element for clearing, novation, or a CCP guarantee. The vocabulary has `Sl`, `Bs`, and `Ad` — which are precisely the DeFi re-inventions of a clearinghouse default waterfall — and nothing for the clearinghouse itself.","DESIGNATED CONTRACT MARKET status and contract SELF-CERTIFICATION: Kalshi files a contract's rules with the CFTC and may list it unless the CFTC objects. The listing authority for a market is a regulatory process. No element.","The CONTRACT RULEBOOK — a natural-language specification of the settlement condition and the named settlement source. This is the actual product being sold and there is no symbol for a rulebook.","Segregated customer funds under CFTC Part 1.25, and FCM/member structure.","The order book is a conventional off-exchange matching engine; even `Ob` (forced) is not honestly available because nothing is on-chain.","The on-chain surface is limited to USDC deposit rails and recent Solana integrations. Essentially the whole protocol is residue."]},"pointer":"/categories/3/protocols/0","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Prediction markets & other (uncategorized large protocols)","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c3:p1","original":{"elements":["Ob","Oa","Rd","Au","Gs","Aw","Up","Gp"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Ob","why":"off-chain signed-order matching with on-chain settlement, not an on-chain book."},{"symbol":"Oa","why":"structurally right (assert, bond, dispute, escalate) but wrong in three ways that matter: the escalation terminates in a UMA TOKEN-HOLDER VOTE with no objective referent and documented voter-stake conflicts (WSJ, May 2026: >50% of votes in most disputed markets from the ten largest wallets, ~1 in 5 disputes had a voter with a stake in the outcome); proposals are now restricted to a WHITELIST, making it a permissioned assertion; and the thing being asserted is an interpretation of prose, not an observation of data. `Oa` names the dispute wrapper and not the resolution."},{"symbol":"Gs","why":"candidate register: gasless relayed trading via proxy wallets is real and load-bearing for the UX."},{"symbol":"Au","why":"the proxy-wallet/relayer pattern is delegated execution scope, but it is operator-run rather than user-configured policy."}],"name":"Polymarket","order_known":true,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama $3.14B volume/30d and $330.8M TVL 2026-08-04 — #1 on-chain prediction market, ~85% of on-chain prediction-market TVL","residue":["CONDITIONAL-TOKEN SPLIT AND MERGE. Deposit $1 of collateral, receive one YES and one NO; return both, get $1 back. This is the single most fundamental primitive in prediction markets — a state-partition of collateral into complementary contingent claims — and NO symbol names it. The nearest is `Py` (principal/yield separation), which splits a claim along TIME; this splits along STATE. I did not force `Py`.","THE MARKET RULEBOOK. The natural-language resolution criteria ('will X happen by date Y, per source Z') is the product. Every dispute is a dispute about text. `Oa` gives an assert-then-dispute wrapper around an oracle answer and nothing about what question is being answered.","THE NEGATIVE-RISK ADAPTER, which converts N independent binary markets into a mutually-exclusive set so that a full basket of NOs is redeemable for N-1 collateral. This is a genuine on-chain mechanism (a constraint-imposing wrapper over conditional tokens) with no symbol.","MARKET CREATION AND LISTING AUTHORITY — who may create a market and under what template.","The admin/UMIP-level resolution OVERRIDE path when the oracle produces a result the operator deems wrong.","The off-chain matching operator (orders are signed and matched by Polymarket, settled on the CTF Exchange) — a censorship and reordering surface `Ob` conceals."]},"pointer":"/categories/3/protocols/1","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Prediction markets & other (uncategorized large protocols)","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c3:p2","original":{"elements":["Sh","Rl","Ex","Sv","Rd","Em","Up","Gp"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Rl","why":"candidate register: the LiquidityTree genuinely reserves a slice of pool liquidity per condition so simultaneous events cannot oversubscribe the same capital — this is the closest good fit in the whole vocabulary. But note that Azuro's own marketing calls it 'concentrated liquidity', which would have made `Cl` an attractive and completely wrong choice: `Cl` is tick-ranged price liquidity, the LiquidityTree is a segment tree over event-level capital allocation. Naming collision, not mechanism match."},{"symbol":"Sv","why":"candidate register: the Data Provider's determination discretion over odds and outcomes is real, but `Sv` is written for loan servicing and does not reach 'sets the price and also decides who won'."},{"symbol":"Ex","why":"a single named data provider pushing odds and results, with no medianizer, no aggregation, and no dispute."}],"name":"Azuro","order_known":true,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama $1.59M TVL 2026-08-04 — largest peer-to-pool (non-order-book) prediction/betting protocol; architecturally distinct from the Polymarket clones above it by volume","residue":["PEER-TO-POOL PAYOFF UNDERWRITING — the same gap found in Hegic. A single LP pool is the counterparty to every bet. Nothing names 'a pool that writes a non-linear payoff'. `Pl` is lending; `Cv` requires adjudicated claims.","ODDS ADJUSTMENT BY POOL EXPOSURE (the vAMM): odds move against incoming flow as a function of the pool's net exposure to that outcome. This is a pricing invariant, and none of `Cp`/`Wg`/`St`/`Cl`/`Pm` describes it — it prices a probability against inventory, not an asset against an asset.","PARLAY / ACCUMULATOR CORRELATION RISK — combining legs multiplies payout but the pool's exposure is not the product of the legs' exposures. A whole risk-management object with no representation.","The Data Provider is a named off-chain party who supplies both the initial odds AND the outcome resolution, with no dispute path. There is no `Oa` here, and `Ex` misrepresents a single trusted party as an oracle."]},"pointer":"/categories/3/protocols/2","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Prediction markets & other (uncategorized large protocols)","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c3:p3","original":{"elements":["Sh","Im","Ct","Wq","Tg","Gp","Fd"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Im","why":"the curator ALLOCATES ACROSS isolated markets; it does not create the risk fence. `Im` describes the substrate, not the vault's mechanism."},{"symbol":"Ct","why":"inherited from the underlying markets, not computed by the vault."},{"symbol":"Fd","why":"candidate register: performance and management fees are taken on-chain."}],"name":"Steakhouse Financial (Risk Curators)","order_known":true,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama $3.08B TVL 2026-08-04 — #1 in the 'Risk Curators' category ($8.76B total, DefiLlama's #9 category overall). Included as a large protocol that fits no conventional DeFi category.","residue":["A DELEGATED DISCRETIONARY ALLOCATION MANDATE. A named firm decides which isolated markets a depositor's capital enters, at what supply cap, and rebalances at will, for a performance fee. This is the entire protocol. No element names it. `Sv` (candidate) is about servicing a loan, not selecting exposures — I declined to force it.","No element for a SUPPLY CAP per market as a risk-budgeting instrument distinct from a collateral threshold.","No element for the curator's LIABILITY or absence of it — depositors bear losses from the curator's choices with no on-chain recourse and no fiduciary encoding.","No element for the fact that the curator's fee is on AUM/performance, creating a documented incentive to reach for yield.","No element for the relationship between the curator layer and the base protocol (Morpho/Euler) — the vault is a client of a market, not a market."]},"pointer":"/categories/3/protocols/3","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"},{"category":"Prediction markets & other (uncategorized large protocols)","legacy_id":"legacy:lane3:c3:p4","original":{"elements":["Sh","Aw","At","Xf","Tg","Gp"],"forced":[{"symbol":"At","why":"the NAV of the off-chain allocation is a manager report, not a protocol-verifiable attestation."},{"symbol":"Xf","why":"cross-chain asset movement is present, but the economically important transfer is CHAIN-TO-BANK, which `Xf` does not describe and no symbol does."}],"name":"Grove Finance (Onchain Capital Allocator)","order_known":true,"rank_basis":"DefiLlama $2.43B TVL 2026-08-04 — #1 in the 'Onchain Capital Allocator' category ($7.74B total, DefiLlama's #12 category). Included as a large protocol that fits no conventional DeFi category.","residue":["Grove takes on-chain capital (largely Sky/Spark) and allocates it into OFF-CHAIN credit — most visibly a Janus Henderson CLO fund. It combines the RWA residue set (obligor, register of record, bankruptcy remoteness, manager discretion) with the curator residue set (allocation mandate, no on-chain recourse). It is the worst case for this vocabulary: two independent gap families stacked.","No element for the mandate: an allocation policy document approved by one DAO governing capital sourced from another.","No element for the CLO tranche structure the capital ultimately buys — `Tr` would name the waterfall if the waterfall were visible, but from Grove's position it is a single opaque NAV.","No element for the redemption LAG between an on-chain instant-liquidity promise and an off-chain fund's monthly redemption window — a structural maturity transformation. `Wq` names a queue; this is a duration mismatch that a queue conceals."]},"pointer":"/categories/3/protocols/4","source_path":"corpus50/lanes/lane3-rwa-options-stables-prediction.json","source_sha256":"94195e7144eb707a7cbe34e4adcbaeeb234a572d7ac485e89ed2636059452820"}],"status":"provisional_source_bound","units":[{"annotation_refs":[{"annotator_id":"a","path":"corpus/normalized/annotations/a.json","pointer":"/annotations/0","sha256":"bef2613e0d4a1b88fcd179a5b051e8eb942610a6299d15e553187705890bc007"},{"annotator_id":"b","path":"corpus/normalized/annotations/b.json","pointer":"/annotations/0","sha256":"b2d30c390da953c464169f805aef1e4bcfaeeec076bc6c235cc6872536a47022"}],"deployment":{"address":null,"chain":null,"source_revision":null,"status":"unresolved"},"evaluation_role":"development","evidence_role":"legacy_context","facets":{"economic_functions":["exchange"],"execution":[],"instruments":["spot_asset"],"mechanisms":["amm","mint_burn"],"trust":[]},"label":"Uniswap","legacy_id":"legacy:lane1:c0:p0","normalization_status":"needs_identity_review","organization":{"id":"org:uniswap","label":"Uniswap","status":"label_only"},"product":{"id":"product:lane1:c0:p0","label":"Uniswap","status":"provisional"},"split_rule":"identity-candidate","uncertainty":["Deployment It is simultaneously the reason the design is safer than holding assets on an exchange and the largest single risk surface in a $3.9B protocol, and 58 symbols say nothing about it.","no element for capturing an off-protocol revenue stream. Pf names the funding transfer that a perp venue implements between its own longs and shorts. Ethena is the taker of someone else's Pf, on a venue it neither operates nor governs. There is no way in this vocabulary to write 'this protocol's entire yield is another protocol's mechanism, received as an external party.'","no element for delta-neutrality as a maintained invariant. The requirement is that net exposure stay at approximately zero, continuously, as spot moves, margin is rebalanced across venues, and positions are rolled. It is an operational obligation on an off-chain operator, checked by no contract.","no element for venue and counterparty concentration, or for what happens to the hedge when an exchange fails while holding it (the FTX case for this design)","no element for mint/redeem being restricted to a whitelist of market makers. Dp reads 'directional position & hedge maintenance'. Ethena's defining property is that it is deliberately NON-directional — the whole design is the absence of direction. And the hedge is not an overlay protecting some other exposure; the hedge IS the reserve asset. Dp captures roughly one thing (a short position is opened and rebalanced) out of five: it is silent on where the position lives (a centralized venue), who maintains it (an off-chain operator), why it exists (to make the backing price-invariant rather than to protect a book), what it earns (funding), and what happens when the venue fails. Score it about 20% coverage of the mechanism it is being asked to name."},{"symbol":"Pf","why":"NOT USED — deliberately. Using Pf here would assert that Ethena runs a perpetual market, which is false. This is a clean directional gap in the vocabulary: every risk-transfer symbol is written from the issuer's side, and there is no way to name being the counterparty."},{"symbol":"Bs","why":"FORCED: the reserve fund absorbs negative funding before anyone else, so it is first-loss. Li presumes a discrete close paid to a third party; nothing here matches.","no element for an automated open-market operations agent. A PegKeeper mints unbacked crvUSD one-sidedly into a stableswap pool when the peg is above 1 and burns it on the way back. The Deposit Security Committee exists solely to stop a griefing attack on the deposit path. This reports state, not prices, and the failure modes are different."},{"symbol":"Bs","why":"FORCED: CSM operators post a slashable ETH bond, an exact fit — but Curated-module operators post nothing at all. Bs is true of one module and false of the majority of the stake, and the vocabulary has no way to scope a symbol to a subset of a protocol."},{"symbol":"Sl","why":"FORCED: slashing and penalty losses reach stETH holders as a negative rebase across the entire supply, regardless of which operator caused them. Rs asserts that restaking exists; it does not name the AVS/operator-set contract, the slashing conditions an AVS is permitted to define, the allocation of a given operator's stake across many AVSs (unique stake / magnitudes), or the fact that the same collateral is simultaneously bonded to mutually-unaware slashing laws.","no element for stake delegation to an operator. The staker to operator to AVS graph is EigenLayer's core object. Au names delegated execution scope (session policy, account abstraction) and is about transaction authority, not about lending someone your slashing exposure. Vl names a validator lifecycle, which an operator is not.","no element for redistributive slashing: slashed stake can be paid to the harmed AVS as restitution rather than burned. Sl assigns loss to a claim class; this assigns it to a counterparty as a remedy, which is a categorically different act.","no element for intersubjective adjudication. EIGEN is forkable as a court of last resort for faults that are observable to humans but not provable on-chain. Oa (optimistic assertion oracle) is the nearest symbol and it describes an on-chain dispute game with a bonded challenger; a social fork of a token is not that.","no element for the allocation/deallocation delay as a security parameter distinct from the withdrawal escrow"],"forced":[{"symbol":"Vl","why":"CANDIDATE, and equivocal. An EigenLayer operator registers, receives delegated stake, performs duties and can be slashed — the lifecycle shape rhymes with a validator's. But there is no consensus duty, no key in a beacon chain, and no protocol-defined job. None of 'Cp', 'Wg', 'St', 'Cl' or 'Pm' describes an invariant that is a function of time. ===== FILE corpus/normalized/sources/README.md | SOURCE SHA256 0f6d62798fb351a5c8ac3cb524394f5abdef1adebf281867c34139438d2e714c | RENDERING verbatim =====
# Limited external provenance capture

The parent harness retrieved the official pages listed in primary-excerpts.json
on the recorded UTC dates. Each record includes the requested/final URL, HTTP
status, content type, response SHA-256, selected excerpts and excerpt SHA-256.
Excerpt normalization removes script/style text, collapses whitespace and removes
spaces immediately before punctuation. Response hashes cover the exact body bytes returned by urllib response.read(),
excluding headers. Excerpt hashes use the UTF-8 encoding of the listed strings
joined with LF and a final LF, without JSON serialization. Each source contributes at most 25 excerpt words.

Full response bytes are not committed; their hashes fingerprint the retrieval
but do not themselves authenticate the publisher or let a future reader recover
a changed page. The current documentation is distinct from the frozen historical
lane narrative and was not shown to the blind annotators. No contract address,
chain deployment or bytecode revision is asserted from this capture.

The original proposal's `sandbox:/mnt/data/defi_kernel_corpus_crosswalk.csv` and
`defi_kernel_taxonomy_schema.json` were not found in the searched accessible home
and Desktop trees. `/mnt/data` was absent. The new corpus/schema are reconstructed
artifacts, and the original proposal's unresolved citation tokens remain open
bibliographic work. This sprint does not claim to have recovered every source.

===== END FILE =====

(3) Uniswap and PancakeSwap differ by exactly two symbols (Em, Up) — PancakeSwap decomposes as 'Uniswap with an emission schedule and a mutable admin', which is a fair summary of the products but erases everything about routing, chains and hook design. Balancer, named in the brief, is now $54.2M combined (V2 $26.7M + V3 $27.5M) — about 1/24th of Curve and nowhere near the top five — and the other live ve-gauge system, Aerodrome, is $247.5M at rank 7. Rough accounting: of ~150 distinct mechanisms I could identify across the 22 protocols, about 110 (73%) took a symbol cleanly, about 20 (13%) took one only as a forced fit, and about 20 (13%) took none at all. But the failure is not evenly spread and the percentage flatters the vocabulary badly, because the residue is concentrated in exactly the mechanisms protocols compete on. It failed hardest in three places. FIRST, the price of credit. There is no element anywhere for a rate — not the utilization curve that every one of six lending protocols runs, not the stability fee and savings rate that every one of five CDPs uses as its primary peg lever, not crvUSD's automatic rate controller, not Liquity V2's borrower-chosen rates. On the 'other' members: DefiLlama's #9 and #12 categories by TVL ($16.5B combined) are curators and allocators, and the vocabulary has zero coverage of a delegated discretionary allocation mandate — the fastest-growing organizational form in DeFi has no symbol.","identical_decompositions":[["Polymarket","Predict Fun / OPINION / InsightX (the #3–#5 on-chain prediction markets by volume, all CTF+CLOB+UMA clones, decompose identically to Polymarket including its residue)"]]}],"completeness_verdict":"Counting rule: for each protocol I enumerated the distinct functional components a competent implementer or risk analyst would have to specify, then counted how many received an unforced symbol. Totals: RWA/private credit ~62 components, ~24 expressible → 39%; Options ~48 components, ~30 expressible → 63%; Fiat stablecoins ~68 components, ~17 expressible → 25%; Prediction/other ~54 components, ~24 expressible → 44%.
